why:
All three checks pass in the finding's favour; the divergence is real. (1) VERBATIM. The quoted sentence exists word-for-word at mcp.md:761, under the heading '### Use dynamic headers for custom authentication'. I read the WHOLE line: it is a two-sentence line and the second sentence REINFORCES rather than reverses — 'Claude Code runs the command and merges its output into the connection headers.' Every element of the claimed behaviour is verbatim-supported in the same section: 'The command must write a JSON object of string key-value pairs to stdout'; 'The command runs in a shell with a 10-second timeout, from the session's current working directory'; 'Dynamic headers override any static `headers` with the same name'; and the env table lists exactly CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME (server name), CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL (server URL) and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT ('Set only when a plugin provides the server'). The field is also documented for ws at mcp.md:147 and listed among plugin server fields at mcp.md:320. So the doc side is not a paraphrase and not cherry-picked.
(2) CITED LINES. Both citations say what was claimed. packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:147-148 is `if (raw.headersHelper !== undefined) { problems.push('"headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored'); }`, preceded by the docblock at :139-143 'headersHelper is READ AND REPORTED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — there is no dynamic header generator anywhere in this codebase for any transport'. packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1058 pushes the warning 'Claude MCP server "<name>" declares headersHelper, which is not implemented for any transport; static headers still apply.' AND `deferred.push({ externalKind: 'mcp', reasonCode: 'plugin.deferred.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported' })` — so the deferred-capability record is real, on the plugin path.
(3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, both layers. Nothing upstream or downstream implements it. Binary-safe `grep -rna --binary-files=text 'headersHelper'` over packages/*/src and apps/*/src returns 25 hits in 6 files and every one is a reader, a docblock, or a test — there is no executor, no spawn, no shell call. `grep -rna --binary-files=text 'CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME|CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL'` over packages, apps and scripts returns ZERO hits, so the documented helper environment is not constructed anywhere. One layer down at the vendored runtime: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js contains headersHelper exactly 3 times (lines 350316, 350319, 350320) and all three are `headersHelper: l3.string().optional()` inside the sse/http/ws zod schemas — the Pi SDK ACCEPTS the field and never consumes it, so no downstream layer silently rescues the behaviour. Our readers strip it before the pool anyway. No sibling-subsystem misnaming is possible: headersHelper is a single MCP-config field name and the only two parsers of it are the two cited.
(4) NOT AN OWNER DECISION. I read all nine dated entries in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). headersHelper is not among them and appears nowhere in that file. It is instead an OPEN, recorded deviation: 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:369 and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-mcp-surfaces.md:117/:142/:154 name it 'documented, not implemented', and the parity audit's N8 row (:726) closes ws transport while leaving this explicitly open.
(5) NOT A FORK PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. headersHelper is transport-level MCP auth, not a Claude/ChatGPT subscription flow, not a rebrand, not gateway-specific. If anything the fork is the doc's own stated audience — 'Kerberos, short-lived tokens, or an internal SSO' is precisely a corporate-gateway deployment.
One correction to the finding's OUR STATE, which makes our position WORSE than claimed, not better, and therefore does not refute it: 'Both readers detect the field and emit a warning' is FALSE for the .mcp.json reader on http and sse. In project-config.ts the headersHelper check sits ONLY inside the `if (type === 'ws')` arm (:144-153); the http/sse arm (:119-134) never touches raw.headersHelper, and parseMcpServersDocument (:190-213) has no generic unknown-key sweep. I proved this with a positive control rather than by reading alone — a temporary bun test through parseMcpServersDocument, since deleted, with the ws case as the control that shows the rig can observe the warning: WS -> ['.mcp.json server "events": "headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored.']; HTTP -> config {"type":"http","url":"https://x.test/mcp"}, warnings []; SSE -> config {"type":"sse","url":"https://x.test/mcp"}, warnings []. So on the transport the doc's own two examples use ('type': 'http'), a project .mcp.json headersHelper is dropped in total silence — the exact failure mode the code comment at :141-143 says it exists to prevent ('an operator ends up debugging a 401 that has nothing to do with their token'). The only test covering that warning, mcp/__tests__/ws-transport.test.ts:46-57, uses type 'ws', which is why the hole survived.
correctedState: Not implemented for any transport, and confirmed unimplemented one layer down as well: the vendored Pi SDK bundle carries `headersHelper` only as an optional zod field on its sse/http/ws schemas (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:350316/350319/350320) and never executes it, and `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME`/`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL` appear nowhere in the repository. The two readers do NOT behave alike, contrary to the original claim. The plugin adapter (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1058) warns for every transport and also files a deferred-capability record (`plugin.deferred.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported`). The project `.mcp.json` reader (packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:147-148) emits its warning ONLY from the `ws` arm; the http/sse arm at :119-134 drops `headersHelper` with no warning at all and no deferred record, and there is no generic unknown-key sweep in parseMcpServersDocument (:190-213) to catch it. Verified empirically against the parser with the ws case as a positive control: ws yields one warning, http and sse yield zero. Since mcp.md documents `headersHelper` primarily for http/sse and both of its examples use `"type": "http"`, the common case is the silent one. Net effect: an http/sse server connects with static headers only and the operator is told nothing; a ws server connects with no headers sent at all (the SDK's WebSocket transport takes only a URL, per parity-audit row N8) but at least names the drop.
